series.name: Drawing with Code
series.playlist_title: Drawing with Code: Manim and ManimOnline
series.playlist_description:
A narrated series about Manim, the Python library for animated math explanations, and ManimOnline, a browser editor that runs a Manim-compatible engine with no install. Episodes 1-9 are for curious beginners who know a little Python; episodes 10-12 are a deep dive into how the editor works. Every QR code on screen opens the exact code in your browser.

This series is independent and is not affiliated with 3Blue1Brown or Manim Community.

0.title: Drawing with Code: Manim and ManimOnline (Trailer)
0.summary:
A dot becomes a line, a circle, a square, a star, and every frame of it is a few lines of Python. This is Manim, the library behind a whole genre of animated math explanations, and ManimOnline, which runs a Manim-compatible engine inside your web browser: no install, no server.

Thirteen episodes take you from your first scene to cameras, 3D, graphs and formulas, then under the hood of the editor itself. Scan the code at the end to edit this trailer's final scene.

1.title: An Animation Is a Program · Drawing with Code 1 (Manim)
1.summary:
A screen can't show motion, only still frames. So who draws all the in-between shapes when a square becomes a circle? In Manim, you don't: you describe the change, and the computer draws every frame.

This episode opens ManimOnline in the browser, tours the editor, reads a first scene line by line (Scene, construct, objects, self.play, self.wait), makes the first edits, and reads an error message without fear.

2.title: Mobjects: The Nouns · Drawing with Code 2 (Manim)
2.summary:
Everything you see in a Manim scene is a mobject. This episode builds the vocabulary: Manim's coordinate plane and direction constants, a zoo of shapes, stroke, fill and opacity, placing things absolutely and relative to each other, scaling, rotating and measuring.

Then the parts that surprise people: groups that move as one, two names for the same object (and when to copy), and who is drawn on top.

3.title: Animations: The Verbs · Drawing with Code 3 (Manim)
3.summary:
Every Manim animation is interpolation driven by one number that runs from 0 to 1. Once you see that, rate functions, built-in animations and timing all make sense.

This episode explains what self.play really does, compares linear, smooth and there-and-back motion, tours the built-in animations, explains why .animate.rotate and Rotate differ (and why a square can shrink to a point), combines animations with AnimationGroup, LaggedStart and Succession, and settles who is on screen after a Transform.

4.title: What Is a Shape, Really? Bézier Curves · Drawing with Code 4 (Manim)
4.summary:
How do you store a circle in a computer? Not as a circle. This episode builds a cubic Bézier curve from nothing but repeated linear interpolation (de Casteljau's construction), then shows how anchors and handles join curves smoothly and why cubics are the standard choice.

A Manim outline turns out to be a list of points in groups of four, and that explains how one shape morphs into another: matching point counts, subdivision, and path_arc.

5.title: Words and Equations: Text, MathTex and Tex · Drawing with Code 5 (Manim)
5.summary:
Text and formulas in Manim are shapes too. This episode chooses between Text, MathTex and Tex, shows how a formula becomes vector outlines (in Manim with LaTeX, and in ManimOnline with MathJax), and indexes letters and formula parts to colour and animate them separately.

Then algebra that moves: TransformMatchingTex, aligned lines of working, braces, titles and TransformFromCopy.

6.title: Things That Change: Updaters and ValueTrackers · Drawing with Code 6 (Manim)
6.summary:
Some things in a scene should follow others: a label that sticks to a dot, a readout that tracks a value, a path traced as something moves. This episode attaches updaters that run every frame, writes time-based updaters with dt, and drives several objects from one ValueTracker.

It also covers always_redraw and TracedPath, the common updater surprises, and how to choose between updaters, trackers, become and plain animations.

7.title: Graphs, Areas and Slopes · Drawing with Code 7 (Manim)
7.summary:
Number lines, axes and plots, built up to calculus you can watch. This episode converts numbers to points, builds Axes and converts with c2p, plots parametric curves and functions (and explains that plots are sampled), and labels them.

Then the payoff: Riemann rectangles converging to an area, an area with a moving bound, a secant line becoming a tangent as dx shrinks, and what a matrix does to the whole plane.

8.title: Cameras and the Third Dimension · Drawing with Code 8 (Manim)
8.summary:
The camera is part of the scene. This episode pans and zooms with MovingCameraScene, shows a magnified inset with ZoomedScene, then steps into 3D: placing the camera with phi and theta, ThreeDAxes, surfaces and solids, and text that stays flat.

It closes with how to keep a 3D scene readable, and how a 3D frame becomes a flat picture.

9.title: From Sketch to Shareable: ManimOnline Tour · Drawing with Code 9
9.summary:
A practical tour of the editor for building something real. Find and load examples in the Sample gallery, choose a scene in a file with several, and understand automatic rendering, Render animation, Cancel render and the limits of the preview.

Then export frames and MP4 or WebM videos, share with a link or save permanently with HashBin, work offline, meet the Graphviz and modl modes, build larger scenes in small checkpointed steps, and know when to move to a full Manim install.

10.title: Python in a Browser Tab: Pyodide and WebAssembly · Drawing with Code 10
10.summary:
Deep dive 1: how a static website runs Python. Why ManimOnline runs Python in your browser rather than on a server; WebAssembly and Pyodide at a conceptual level; why Python runs in a Web Worker and why only the page can stop it.

Then fresh namespaces, stale-result guards, and one render followed all the way from source code to frame data, SVG and an encoded video.

11.title: Rebuilding an Engine to Match Manim · Drawing with Code 11
11.summary:
Deep dive 2: ManimOnline can't run real Manim in the browser, so it brings its own engine, manim-lite. How do you know it's right? This episode defines compatibility as observable behaviour that has to be measured, and shows four ways manim-lite is compared with Manim Community, frame for frame.

Along the way: surprising behaviours a faithful reimplementation must copy, and a clear statement of what manim-lite is not.

12.title: Links That Carry Code: Compression, Hashes and QR Codes · Drawing with Code 12
12.summary:
Deep dive 3, and the series finale: how a link or a QR code can carry a program with no server of its own. Code inside the link, compressed with back-references (the Lempel-Ziv idea); where links run out; cryptographic hashes and the avalanche effect.

Then the anatomy of a HashBin content address, why content-addressed links suit printed QR codes and what can still go wrong, and how the editor keeps itself available offline.
